column2: The warrior order of Ursun, the Father of Bears. Its riders are sworn to the god of the steppe and the hunt, and they ride first when the north comes south. Every bear brother has faced a bear on foot with only a spear. Some of them carry the scars.
The First of the Circle leads Ursun's warriors and speaks for them to the High Speaker and the crown.

The council of Kislev's nobility, where old boyar houses, the crown's new druzhina and the rich guild masters of Erengrad trade favours, marriages and contracts. Nothing in Kislev is decided in the Duma. Everything is decided after it.
The Voice of the Duma speaks for the boyars before the throne, and is the one the Tzar(ina) listens to, or has strangled.
Take your place among the bear brothers, or among the Champions.
Take a better seat in the Duma.
Hunt a bear by Ursun's law: on foot, with a spear, and alone at the end. No dogs and no bows. A Rider of the Rota must make such a kill to become a bear brother.
Hold a feast for Ursun's waking, with mead, a bear dance and a contest of strength. Once a year.
Prove yourself worthy to be a Bear Champion: ride north against a Chaos champion, ride south with the Gryphon Legion, or hold a stanitsa against the raiders.
Call a rota of winged lancers to your banner. They ride home when the war ends.
Join the Rota of the Dawn

Take a posting with the Rota of the Dawn, the riders who guard Dazh's temples and his senior priests. They give up the war rota for the temple guard, and they stand nearer the Ice Court than the Orthodoxy.
You join the Rota of the Dawn. You can no longer call a war rota, but you can set the Dawn's guard on your lord and the temple of the capital.
Set the Rota of the Dawn to guard your lord and the temple of the capital for ten years.
Call every bear brother of the Circle to war. Bear riders and axemen march under your banner until the peace.
Take on a task for the Duma to rise in it: a marriage to broker, a town to rebuild, a contract to win or a speech before the crown.
Feast the boyars around you: meat, mead and a hunt. They will remember who fed them.
Raise this courtier to the druzhina, the crown's new nobility, and give them a seat in the Duma. The old families will not like it.
Petition the Tzar(ina) for tax relief or the crown's favour.
Call the boyars of the Duma together.
Ward your lord's capital with ice for five years. The walls grow slick, the gates freeze shut, and raiders find easier prey.
Has slain a bear by Ursun's law
There is a free place in the next rank
Has not hunted a bear in the last three years
Has not held a Waking Day feast this year
Has not taken a trial or task in the last five years
Has not called a rota in the last five years
Has not set the Dawn's guard in the last ten years
Has not mustered the Circle in the last ten years
Has not hosted a great feast in the last five years
Has not petitioned the crown in the last ten years
Has not convened the Duma in the last ten years
Has not raised anyone to the druzhina in the last five years
Has not cast a Frost Ward in the last five years
Has hunted a bear by Ursun's law recently.
Has held a Waking Day feast this year.
Has taken a society trial or task recently.
Has set the Rota of the Dawn's guard recently.
Has hosted a great feast recently.
Has raised someone to the druzhina recently.
Has cast a Frost Ward recently.
Away in the south with the Gryphon Legion, Kislev's winged lancers.
Blessed at the Waking Day feast. The Father of Bears is awake and watching.
Lost a fight with a bear, and has the scars to prove it.
Riders of the Rota of the Dawn guard this lord day and night.
The Tzar(ina) has granted relief from the crown's taxes.
The Tzar(ina) has shown this boyar favour before the whole court.
Keeps the Ice Palace whole with her magic.
Riders of the Rota of the Dawn guard the temple of Dazh here.
An Ice Witch has warded this place. The walls are slick with ice and the gates are frozen shut.
The pelt of a great bear killed on foot by Ursun's law. It is heavy enough to stop an arrow and warm enough to sleep in the snow.
A bear's claw bound in silver wire, given by the Circle to those who pass its trials.
A chain of silver filigree from the jewellers of Praag, so fine it looks like frost.
A long kaftan of black sable trimmed with gold. Only a great boyar would dare wear it before the Tzar(ina).

The hunters found the tracks at dawn, and now the bear stands up out of the bracken in front of you, taller than a mounted man. The beaters have fallen back as Ursun's law says they must. It is you, your spear and the bear.
Set the spear and meet it.

The bear comes down on the spear with all its weight, and the shaft bends but holds. It dies with its jaws a hand's breadth from your face. When the hunters come back they find you sitting against its side, laughing. Tonight its heart is yours to eat.
The spear glances off a rib and the bear is on you. You remember the weight of it, the stink and the claws. You do not remember being carried home. The healers say you will live.

You lower the spear. The bear drops to all fours, looks at you for a long moment, and walks away into the trees. The priest who came with the hunt is on his knees. He says Ursun himself has spared you.

To become a Bear Champion you must prove yourself before the whole Circle. The old champions offer three roads: ride north into the Wastes and kill a champion of Chaos, ride south with the Gryphon Legion and win glory in the Empire, or hold a stanitsa on the steppe when the raiders come.
A champion of the Dark Gods has come out of the Wastes looking for a worthy foe. He waits on a frozen river, in armour of black iron that smokes in the cold, and he laughs when he sees you.
You ride south with the winged lancers of the Gryphon Legion. Ahead lies a season of war in the Empire. You will not be back before the snows come twice.
The riders came in at dusk with the news: raiders out of the north, a hundred of them or more, riding for the stanitsa at the river bend. There are thirty men behind the stockade and you.
Hold the walls until they break.
The champion of Chaos lies dead on the ice. You hack the head from his body and carry it back to the Circle on your spear. The old champions bang their cups on the table until the hall shakes.
You come home with the Gryphon Legion's thanks and a scar for every battle. The Legion's captain has written to the Circle. The old champions say you rode like a winged lancer born.
At dawn the raiders broke and fled back to the north, and the stanitsa still stood. The villagers have already made a song about you. It is not a very good song, but they sing it loud.
The champion of Chaos was too strong. You came to on the ice with his laughter in your ears and your blood freezing around you. He left you alive. That was the insult.
The Legion's season went badly. You came home early on a cart, with a southern surgeon's stitches in your side and nothing to show the Circle.
The stanitsa burned. You got the women and children out, but the Circle does not count a burned stanitsa as a trial won.

Ursun is awake! The snow is melting off the steppe and the whole court has turned out for Waking Day. There is mead, a bear dance around the fire and a contest of strength for the young men. They are waiting for you to begin.
An old bear brother is dead, and the Circle burns him on the steppe with his axe and his horse. The young riders watch the flames. The old men pass a skin of kvas from hand to hand.
Speak for him at the pyre.
Sit and drink with the old men.
A young rider of the rota, all shoulders and no beard, stands up in front of the whole Circle and challenges you to wrestle. The hall goes quiet.
Sit down before you hurt yourself.
A senior priest of Dazh must travel to the temple at Kislev, and the Rota of the Dawn rides with him. On the third night wolves come out of the snow, and something bigger than a wolf behind them.

Water is dripping in the Ice Palace. The one who sits the Ice Throne is no Ice Witch, and without one the palace slowly melts. A courier from the crown asks if you will come and hold it whole with your magic. It is hard, cold work, and the crown will not thank you for long.
Let it drip. It is not my palace.

Two great boyar houses want to join their blood, but neither trusts the other an inch. Both have asked you to arrange the match. There are dowries to haggle, old insults to forget and a bride who has said she would rather marry a bear.
Raiders burned a town on the Lynsk last winter. The Duma has promised to rebuild it, and someone must pay the masons. Whoever does will have a street named after them, and a seat higher up the table.
A merchant house from Marienburg wants a contract for amber and furs. The Duma wants it too, on its own terms, and you have been chosen to win it.
The Duma has chosen you to speak for it before the throne. The boyars want lower taxes and fewer druzhina. The crown wants neither. You must find words that will not end with you in a dungeon.
The wedding was magnificent, and both houses think they got the better bargain. The Duma counts it to your credit.
The town on the Lynsk is rising again, and the main street has your name. The Duma counts it to your credit.
The contract is signed, on the Duma's terms, and the Marienburger left thinking it was his idea. The Duma counts it to your credit.
You spoke well. The crown granted a little, the boyars won a little, and nobody was strangled. The Duma counts it to your credit.
The bride ran away with a horse trader the night before the wedding. Both houses blame you.
The masons took your money and the town is still a ruin. Someone has drawn a rude picture of you on the town gate.
The Marienburger signed with the Erengrad guilds instead. The Duma will not forget it.
Your speech fell flat. The crown was bored, the boyars were embarrassed, and someone laughed.
The boyars have come from all around for your feast. There are roast boar and swans, sturgeon from the Lynsk and rivers of mead, and a hunt in the morning for anyone who can still ride.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come before the throne for the Duma with a petition. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks for relief from the crown's taxes, or failing that, a sign of your favour before the court.
The crown has granted your petition: your lands are relieved of the crown's taxes for five years.
The crown has honoured you before the whole court. Everyone saw it.
The crown has refused your petition, and the court saw that too.
The boyars of the Duma have gathered at your call, in sables and gold chains, and every one of them has a grievance. They are waiting for the Voice of the Duma to speak.
The Duma will pay a levy.

At a Duma dinner an old boyar raises his cup and mocks the druzhina at the end of the table: upstarts in borrowed furs, whose grandfathers herded pigs. The druzhina have their hands on their knives. Everyone is looking at you.
He is right. Blood is blood.
The crown's men are as good as any boyar.

A Gospodar boyar and an Ungol ataman have come to your court to quarrel over the summer grazing. The Gospodar has the charters. The Ungol has the horses, and has had them there since before the Gospodars came.
The charter stands. The Gospodar wins.
The grass belongs to the horses. The Ungol wins.
A guild master from Erengrad has left a heavy purse on your table and asked a small favour of the Duma: a word in the right ear about a harbour tax.
A small favour, for a friend.
